title: Enoch
summary: Seventh from Adam; walked with God and was taken by God without dying.

sorting_basis.note: Tier 4: Ussher, Annals: 622 AM, 3382 BC (no higher-tier year available).

birth.citation: Jones, Chronology of the Old Testament (15th ed., 2002), "Chronological Compendium", p. 1
birth.note: Jones prints only the AM figure here; no BC year is printed for this birth, so year_bc_ad is left null (not inferred).

birth.citation: Gen 5 cumulative begetting ages (father jared begat at 162, Gen 5:18)
Ussher, Annals of the World, First Age, §18 (paragraph numbering of the modern transcription)
Jordan, "The Chronology of the Pentateuch (Part 2)," Biblical Chronology 6:4 (April 1994), §4 "The Chronology of Genesis 4 & 5" (year list)

birth.date: 622 AM (birth year printed at the start of the Enoch bar)
birth.citation: Anno Mundi Chronology Studies (unnamed compiler; a compilation of James B. Jordan's system), p. 1, chart "A.M. Chronology (Anno Mundi “Year of the World”) Genesis 5, 11:10"
birth.note: Agrees with Jordan's own published AM 622.

birth.citation: Raleigh, The History of the World (1617, EEBO-TCP A10357), Chronological Table, sig. 781b
birth.note: Year cell "1305 623". To the Reader (sig. 780b): the Julian Period exceeds the yeere of the World by 682. The 265 at the end of the name is the lifespan he prints. His table also prints the translation at World 987. 623 + 265 is not 987. Both figures are left as printed.

translated.note: Not stated in the Jones sources read (Chart No. 1; Chronology of the Old Testament 15th ed. 2002, Chronological Compendium p. 1). Leave empty until verified.
Enoch did not die: "he was not; for God took him" (Gen 5:24; Heb 11:5).

translated.citation: Ussher, Annals of the World, First Age, §22 (paragraph numbering of the modern transcription)
translated.note: Ussher: "translated by God in an instant ... that he should not see death."
